heard: Four astronauts will fly 252,756 miles to break Apollo 13's record. Slated for 2026, aboard NASA's Space Launch System, Artemis II will push farther into deep space than humans have ever traveled. Commander Reed Weissman and pilot Victor Glover will guide the Orion spacecraft integrity on this 10-day flight. ESA's European Service Module provides the power to loop the crew around the lunar far side. Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen join Victor Glover as the first woman, non-American, and black astronaut to fly around the moon. While Apollo 13 reached its record during a crisis, Artemis II will reach it as a planned trial run. After splashing down in the Pacific, this flight will reset the record for the farthest humans have ever traveled.
